races.name: Racedays For 9 Pound At Nottingham Racecourse Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cosmic Mystery
runners_data.comment: Undersized but sprint-bred and sharp, rated the best of this quintet on 82, she should take a real step forward once she gets a second completed run under her, having unseated at Redcar last time. Effective at 5f, and today's faster ground suits her ideally. The yard is without a winner from 31 runners in the last fortnight, but she looks clear of this field on the balance of the facts.

runners_data.name: Glamorize
runners_data.comment: Below her best when beaten 9 1/4 lengths in a Group 3 at Ascot last time, plainly out of her depth in that grade, but drops back appreciably today and wears cheekpieces for the first time. Effective at 5f on quick ground, with the yard among the in-form stables currently. Rates a leading threat back at a suitable level.

runners_data.name: Lion Of Persia
runners_data.comment: Green and never able to land a blow on his only start, a well-beaten eighth in a novice at Windsor last time. He's bred for speed and there should be more to come with that experience now banked, but he needs it given the modest form shown so far. Rated bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: One In A Millz
runners_data.comment: Stepped forward from his debut when beaten 9 lengths in a novice at this course last time, though the form was still modest, and there's plenty more needed to be competitive here. Bred for speed and open to more with racing experience, but the yard is out of form currently at just 4% over the last fortnight. Rated a workable contender rather than a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Articulate
runners_data.comment: This colt changed hands for £5,000 as a juvenile and is bred for speed - by the smart sprinter Showcasing out of Dutch Treat, herself a useful sprinter, with a half-brother in Perfect Spring who was useful at 6f. This yard isn't renowned for first-time winners, but he looks sharp enough for 5f. Untested, with plenty still to find out.

races.name: Ivor Thirst Sprint Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Mariselle
runners_data.comment: Her debut at Lingfield was full of promise - travelling strongly into the race before fading late to fourth, beaten 7 1/4 lengths, and she looked to have grasped the basics quickly. With that experience banked there should be more to come, and she's proven over today's trip and goes well on good ground. Rated a leading threat on these figures.

runners_data.name: Miracleoftheandes
runners_data.comment: Sent off well fancied for her second start, she set a strong pace at Newbury before weakening out of contention late, fourth beaten 7 lengths. That was almost a year ago and she'll need to progress to figure again, but she is proven over today's trip and ground. A modest profile that leaves her with plenty to prove back after a long spell off.

runners_data.name: Shego
runners_data.comment: An unraced daughter of Eqtidaar out of a mare who was useful at 7f at two but without a win of her own, and with the yard among the in-form stables currently. This experience alone may be what she needs before she shows her best. Rated highly on our figures, but she remains unproven in a race environment.

runners_data.name: Sugar Bon Bon
runners_data.comment: Race keen and never landed a blow when well beaten in a novice at Catterick latest, with the figures (8th, 5th) pointing to a horse who needs more to find. Bred for more of a test than today's minimum trip offers, which is unlikely to play to his strengths. Rated near the foot of this field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Tide Runner
runners_data.comment: Forced to switch and short of a change of gear when well beaten in a maiden at Ayr latest, with the soft ground possibly not helping his cause. A quicker surface today should suit, given he acts on sound going and is proven at this minimum trip. Recent figures (7th, 3rd) still leave plenty to find, and he's rated only a place chance.

runners_data.name: Courageous Sioux
runners_data.comment: Struggling for pace and green early on her debut at Thirsk, this filly was some way off it before finishing well enough once she began to travel, beaten 5 lengths. That experience should help, especially with this yard renowned for sharpening horses for a second start, and she returns from a long absence but is proven over today's trip. Rated a leading threat on these figures.

runners_data.name: Court Alert
runners_data.comment: Useful at two but inconsistent since, and the four-length fourth at Brighton latest carries an excuse - denied a clear run, he had little left in space, understandable in just his second start back from wind surgery. Drops to the minimum trip on quick ground, and more to come. Winless in five, but rated the one to beat.

runners_data.name: El Ghuwah
runners_data.comment: Unraced newcomer, a 1,000gns Mohaather gelding whose family carries residual promise - half-brother Gordon Norse was useful at 7f and successful second time out. With no form of his own, the market may be the best guide on debut, and this looks stiff company to open in. Rated only a fringe player.

runners_data.name: Green Champion
runners_data.comment: A well-related newcomer by the sprint influence Mehmas out of the smart sprinter Lady Of The Desert, and a half-brother to Queen Kindly, useful at 6f. This yard is adept at readying juveniles first time out, and the minimum trip looks his likely metier. Unexposed, with more expected than the figures currently show, but everything to prove.

races.name: Gold Star Gallop Handicap

runners_data.name: Charlie Boyo
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's 3yo has solid course-appropriate form including a recent runner-up at 5f on good, but is a confirmed hold-up horse who is likely to be forced closer than he'd like given the volume of similar runners in this field, which must temper his prospects.
runners_data.comment: Missed the break and was ridden hard to make up the deficit in a handicap at Windsor last time, understandably running out of steam to finish well beaten, 8 1/4 lengths back. Once a useful sort at two over the minimum trip on quick ground, he presumably had some issue along the way and has that ability still to confirm. A first-time tongue-tie is fitted, but he's rated bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Duskaura
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll sends this filly back after 15 days with a solid recent fourth on good ground, though her five career runs have been entirely at 5f and this 6f trip is an unexplored question; she's a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield slot on the map.
runners_data.comment: Conditions at a tight track worked against her last time, beaten 3 lengths off a 2lb higher mark at Goodwood, though the effort was true to her current form. She hasn't been at her sharpest of late and her mark keeps easing, but she's suited by the minimum trip and acts on a range of going, including today's. A leading contender on these figures.

runners_data.name: Macanudo
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's 5yo has been campaigned exclusively at 6-7f on standard ground and switches to turf and faster conditions here, a combination he hasn't encountered in recent starts — his staying-on-from-the-back style is the one least able to exploit Zarinca's likely controlled tempo.
runners_data.comment: Missing the break forced early exertions that left little in reserve, and he faded down the field in a handicap at Southwell most recently, with more needed to be competitive here. He's effective across 5f-7f, but the yard is misfiring badly at present, managing just a single winner from 47 runners in the last fortnight. Rated an each-way player at best.

runners_data.name: Eartha
runners_data.note: 351 days off the track is an enormous lay-off flag for Richard & Peter Fahey's 4yo, and even though she shaped with promise in a 4th on good 6f before her break, the fitness question combined with a natural hold-up style makes her a significant risk in a race that may not produce a scorching pace to deliver her.
runners_data.comment: A well below-par effort in a handicap at Haydock last time, beaten 7 1/4 lengths and never landing a blow, is the most recent evidence, and there have evidently been underlying issues since. Nearly a year off the track now, she may be worth simply monitoring rather than backing on this return, though she is proven over today's trip and going. Winless in four, with plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Acclaimed Freedom
runners_data.note: George Scott's 3yo is a genuine hold-up horse with a recent win at 7f on standard and a 2nd at 6f, and crucially has no redistribution flag — this horse can legitimately race from the rear without compromise, which makes it the cleanest beneficiary if the pace fractions suit a late run.
runners_data.comment: Back down in trip suited him last time, and he progressed again to be beaten only a neck off a 2lb lower mark at Windsor, continuing an upward curve that includes a win earlier in the sequence. A promising sort whose breathing issue looks to have been resolved, he's effective at 6f and stretches out well to 7f, with the yard among the in-form stables. Rated clear of this field and the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Zarinca
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, ridden by Paul Mulrennan for Edward Bethell, and her course and distance win on standard ground gives her a structural edge — on good-to-firm she has a single run showing 1/4 sim-going, and she's asked to do it from the front solo, which is the dominant tactical narrative of this race shape.
runners_data.comment: A handicap debut at Pontefract came too soon after a break, and she paid for it late on, beaten 6 lengths, though that experience should bring improvement now. She already has a win under her belt this term, but remains unproven on turf having made her mark on the all-weather so far. Effective at 6f, and unexposed enough to progress from here.

runners_data.name: Emperor Caradoc
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old Paul Midgley handicapper with three wins at 6f on good in recent history (hg:p flags prior hood use) and a course record showing 1/6f/GOO in his last five — his prominent tendencies mean he is the horse most naturally placed to sit on Zarinca's shoulder and challenge in the final 2f.
runners_data.comment: A winner of this race twelve months ago, and successful by a half-length off the same mark at Thirsk in May, he's since held his form without adding to that tally, running to par in sixth, beaten 2 lengths, off 75 last time. First-time cheekpieces go on, and he's effective at 5f-6f on any going. The mark now asks more, but he's a leading player.

runners_data.name: Beyond Borders
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's 5yo has a win at 6f on good and similar ground (hg:tp — tongue-tie and hood), but as a hold-up horse pushed onto the map in a midfield position he cannot easily replicate the prominent role his best run suggests — his redistribution status is a meaningful discount to his prospects.
runners_data.comment: Successful by a head off a 5lb lower mark at Wolverhampton two starts back, he's continued that upward curve, running to form again when second, beaten just a half-length, off 1lb less than he carries today. Full of confidence on his last couple of starts and race-fit over course and distance, he wears both a tongue-tie and cheekpieces for the first time. Effective at 6f on any ground, he holds obvious claims off what looks a fair mark.

races.paceDynamic: Zarinca is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Nottingham, and with no other genuine pace horse to challenge her, she should be able to dictate a controlled, metronomic gallop from the outset rather than being dragged into a war for the lead. The remainder of the field — Charlie Boyo, Duskaura, Macanudo, Eartha, Beyond Borders and Acclaimed Freedom — are all natural hold-up horses, with Emperor Caradoc showing prominent tendencies in his form history (hg:p), meaning Zarinca's ability to set her own tempo unchallenged is the defining structural feature of this race. This field holds far more hold-up types than the track map can accommodate at the rear; in practice, Charlie Boyo, Duskaura, and Beyond Borders are among the most likely to push forward and take a closer position than their natural style dictates, compressing the midfield. A controlled, uncontested lead at honest-but-not-scorching pace on fast ground strongly favours a horse that can travel handy, sustain its effort through the final 2f, and not require a late sprint off a truly hot gallop — the prominent-to-midfield profile with a proven finishing kick is best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zarinca Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca is allowed to dictate a smooth, uncontested gallop throughout and the pace is honest but never punishing.
scenarios.body: Zarinca sets the fractions on her own terms over the 6f, racing across the stands rail, and her rivals in the hold-up group are left with just enough time in the straight to mount a challenge but not enough ground to run past a horse travelling fluently.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Down Late
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca's solo lead is slightly faster than it looks and hold-up horses who push forward find enough momentum through the dip to reel her in.
scenarios.body: The pace proves more taxing than appearances suggest on the quick ground, and a horse that has genuinely tracked just off the pace — rather than being caught wide or flat-footed — picks up strongly in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, True Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca is pressed earlier than expected by rivals shuffling forward out of role and the whole field ends up racing faster than ideal.
scenarios.body: The early surge creates a fast early pace that burns off the pace-setters, leaving the race wide open at the 2f pole for any horse with residual energy; however, most runners here are redistributed hold-up types unlikely to truly benefit because they will have been pushed closer than they want.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Pull Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Zarinca and Emperor Caradoc — who has course-winning form and prominent tendencies — break sharply and the pair race clear of a field that fails to organise quickly.
scenarios.body: The two most prominent horses race in tandem through the opening exchanges, creating a breakaway that the hold-up pack cannot bridge from their backpedalled positions; the winner emerges from within that front duo.

watchPoints.text: Zarinca's solo lead is the fulcrum of this race — watch whether Paul Mulrennan is allowed to stride clear uncontested or if Charlie Boyo or Beyond Borders push up to pressure her in the first 2f, which would fundamentally change the race shape.

Emperor Caradoc has won three of his last five at 6f on good ground at this course — if he travels smoothly just off Zarinca's heels, he represents the most dangerous threat to her lead and must be monitored through the dip.

Eartha is 351 days absent and must be treated with caution; if she shows early signs of ring-rustiness or is pushed further back than her trainer intends, she is effectively a non-factor regardless of the pace shape.

The going report consistently records this 6f contest as Good to Firm despite the race card listing Good — faster ground slightly aids a horse travelling prominently and sustaining, rather than a closer needing a strong pace to be delivered.

Several hold-up horses — particularly Duskaura and Charlie Boyo — may drift forward in the early stages out of role, which could compress the midfield and inadvertently create a pocket for Acclaimed Freedom to slide through on the inside if a gap opens in the straight.

races.name: Nottingham's Finest Ale Mile Handicap

runners_data.name: Jack Langley
runners_data.note: Clear pace-setter here with a recent win at 13f on good going and three placings at 12f; uncontested lead on good-to-firm suits his prominent style perfectly, though his last run over 16f at Sandown produced a poor sixth and stamina at this trip is the only genuine query.
runners_data.comment: Won by four lengths at Lingfield last time, stepping up in trip to beat an in-form rival for a yard that's firing, and he's only risen 6lb for it. Stays this two-mile trip, handles good ground, and rates the one to beat on our figures.

runners_data.name: Saratoga Gold
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran with four places from nine starts on similar going, and a course of 16f suits his staying profile; natural hold-up type who has been placed twice at this sort of trip on good-to-firm, though the trainer is 0/10 in the past 14 days and the headgear (blinkers) has not sparked a return to his best recently.
runners_data.comment: A keen-going sort well beaten in a Kempton handicap last time after over-racing, undoing a run of closer efforts; first-time blinkers may settle him. Winless in five starts but proven over today's trip and ground, he'd take plenty of catching back on that better form.

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: Trainer Ian Williams is 5/28 in the past fortnight which is a solid strike-rate, but this horse's flat form at 12-14f on good has been poor (three finishes of 9th, 16th, 9th) and a flag for fading in the finish is a serious concern at 1m6f; genuine hold-up type whose map placement in midfield reflects the crowded rear — do not take the mapped position as his natural zone.
runners_data.comment: Struggled up in trip when beaten nine lengths in a Sandown handicap last time, and this new yard has little to go on beyond a flash of promise in Meydan, leaving him with plenty to find off this mark. Suited around today's trip, but with just one modest placing from four runs, he's hard to trust on figures.

runners_data.name: Ikigai Star
runners_data.note: 309 days off the track (53 career jumps runs noted) raises a significant fitness flag, but when last seen on turf over similar distances he posted back-to-back thirds at 18f and 20f on good ground, and two wins from 12 similar-going starts suggest capability; hood fitted and David Nolan is a positive booking if the horse shows up in condition.
runners_data.comment: A dual-purpose sort who raced up with the pace and worked hard through the first half before being pulled up in a hurdles handicap at Hereford last time, form easily forgiven. First-time visor and a workable mark on his hurdling form add appeal, and he's proven over today's trip and ground off a quick turnaround.

runners_data.name: Chambers
runners_data.note: 222 days since last run is a concern for a horse whose five recent outings have yielded no finish better than fourth; natural hold-up type whose consistent finishes in sixth and seventh over 14-16f on good ground indicate limited scope for improvement — the midfield slot in the map is a product of redistribution, not his preferred approach to a race.
runners_data.comment: Continuing an inconsistent run across both codes, he never travelled and looked green when well beaten in a Warwick maiden hurdle latest. Best form has come at shorter trips on the all-weather, and without a win in five he's hard to fancy over today's stiffer 14f test.

runners_data.name: Regally Blonde
runners_data.note: Jonny Peate takes the ride on a seven-year-old who has finished sixth, fifth, seventh, seventh, and tenth in her last five — a pattern of near-miss and retreat rather than late threat; fitted with a hood, which may sharpen early focus, but her true preference to come from behind leaves her dependent on honest pace that this race shape is unlikely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Fitted with first-time cheekpieces, she was successful in this same contest a year ago and already boasts course, trip and today's ground form. Below her best this season and beaten seven lengths at Windsor last time without excuse, she nonetheless remains capable of running well again today.

races.paceDynamic: Jack Langley is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of six over 1m6f on good-to-firm ground at Nottingham, and with no rival likely to dispute his lead, he should control tempo from the outset at a pace entirely of his own choosing. The remaining five runners — Saratoga Gold, Free World, Ikigai Star, Chambers, and Regally Blonde — are all natural hold-up or prominent types, yet three of them (Free World, Chambers, Regally Blonde) are redistributed in the map because there is simply not enough room at the rear for every genuine closer; they may be forced further forward than ideal. With Jack Langley dictating an unchallenged, measured gallop over a staying trip, the race is unlikely to develop the strong, relentless pace that true hold-up horses need to deliver their best finishing efforts. This shape strongly favours either Jack Langley himself if he can sustain his lead, or a horse that can sit prominently just off the uncontested leader and produce a controlled, grinding finish — Saratoga Gold and Ikigai Star, both genuine hold-up types with stamina profiles, are best positioned to exploit what pace there is.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Langley Dictates, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Langley leads unchallenged at a sustainable pace and the field fails to reel him in over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Langley sets a comfortable tempo, never extending himself, and the scattered hold-up horses behind him face the classic handicapper's dilemma of insufficient early pace to set up a late charge; with no rival applying pressure, he simply runs his rivals into the ground on good-to-firm ground that suits. His recent win at this trip on similar going and strong style fit for the position he will actually occupy make this the dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stayer Sweeps Late
scenarios.trigger: If Langley sets a slightly stronger-than-expected gallop and one genuine hold-up stayer finds enough cover to produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: Ikigai Star, with solid form over 18-20f on good ground and a record of two wins from 12 similar-going starts, is the most credible beneficiary of any meaningful pace injection, as the longer trip and flat course suit her stamina. Saratoga Gold, placed four times in similar conditions, could also come home strongly if the fractions are honest enough to bring hold-up horses into play.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Collide
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed horses — Free World, Chambers, Regally Blonde — are forced to race closer than their natural style and traffic problems or crowding disrupt the finish.
scenarios.body: These three genuine hold-up horses, squeezed into midfield by the tactical shape, could find themselves shuffled wider or checked at a critical point, but any one of them tracking the leader more prominently than intended could accidentally inherit a winning position if Langley fades sharply in the final furlong. Regally Blonde, fitted with a hood, is the wildcard here, though inconsistent form limits confidence, and all three carry STYLE_FIT discounts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Langley Fades, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Langley overcooks the early pace or is unable to maintain his effort over the extra 2f, causing a late scramble among a field poorly positioned to take advantage.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses, strung out at unhelpful distances, would be hard-pressed to produce a coordinated late surge, but whoever is closest at the two-furlong pole inherits the advantage; this is the least structured of outcomes and relies on multiple things going wrong simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Jack Langley's stamina at 1m6f is unproven at the top of the trip — watch whether Rowan Scott keeps him relaxed through the first mile, as any early scrappiness could cost him the final furlong.
Ikigai Star has been off for 309 days; watch the market moves and paddock behaviour closely — if fresh, she has strong staying form at 18-20f, but cold and ring-rusty she could be a false price.

Free World is flagged as a horse that fades in the finish; if Paul Mulrennan pushes him forward earlier than natural to avoid being last, watch for him to stop quickly inside the final quarter-mile and cause interference.

The going is confirmed good-to-firm for this race despite the card header showing Good — horses with turf form on quick ground (Jack Langley, Ikigai Star) have an edge over those whose best form has come on softer surfaces.

Three redistributed hold-up horses (Free World, Chambers, Regally Blonde) racing closer than ideal could bunch between the 3f and 2f poles — watch for any crowding or checking on the home turn that might inconvenience Saratoga Gold or Ikigai Star tracking just behind them.

races.name: Shipstones 1852 Heritage Cup Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Celestias Comet
runners_data.note: Fanshawe-trained hold-up filly with three runs at similar good-ground conditions producing one place; 25 days since last run is manageable but her recent form figures of 0-6655 suggest limited progress, and she races from a high weight of 135lbs which bites harder in a sprint finish.|
runners_data.comment: A modest run of five without a win includes a comfortable defeat back on turf at Brighton last time, beaten 6 lengths in a handicap, and there's more needed on this evidence. Her mark keeps drifting the right way, though, and the yard is among the in-form stables, while a first-time hood may add a touch of sharpness. Effective around today's trip on quick ground, but others hold stronger claims on figures.

runners_data.name: Phaedra
runners_data.note: Three wins from fifteen on comparable going and a placed effort over ten furlongs at Nottingham recently give her the most relevant course-and-distance profile in this field; Joey Ramsden's yard is firing at 2/10 in the past fortnight and Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim is a genuine asset in a low-grade fillies' handicap.|
runners_data.comment: Frequently in the frame without going one better across six runs, this filly bounced back into form when fitted with a first-time tongue-tie last time, keeping on for a 3-length defeat at Doncaster off the same mark she carries today. She raced free but the headgear evidently helped settle her, and she is suited by this longer trip on a sound surface. A workable mark and clear claims among the principals.

runners_data.name: Huggable
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's filly arrives on decent recent form (220-69) but her natural inclination is to race from the rear — shown in midfield on the map simply because the field overloads the hold-up positions, and she will need a pace that materialises to make that style work on good-to-firm turf; STYLE_FIT of 0.91 is a meaningful caution.|
runners_data.comment: Still to hit form this campaign, and stepping up in trip did her no favours when down the field in a handicap at Salisbury last time. She's better suited back around 10f, with soft ground bringing out her best, though the yard is out of form currently at just 3% over the last fortnight. Others look to hold stronger claims on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Saliko
runners_data.note: Pressed into the front-running role by default with no natural pace-setter in the race, though her natural style tag is hold-up and her STYLE_FIT of 0.80 is the weakest in the field; Jack Jones's yard is at 0/8 in the past two weeks, and her form of 0-7940 offers little encouragement if the lead role doesn't suit her temperament.|
runners_data.comment: An inconsistent sort who nonetheless has looked a big player two runs back, this filly gets cheekpieces for the first time today after a moderate effort down the field in a handicap at Wolverhampton last time. She is suited by this longer trip on a sound surface, and the headgear could be the key to unlocking her best. Winless in five, but rated clear of this field on figures.

runners_data.name: Rosemary May
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly carries the lightest weight burden of the serious contenders at 121lbs and has recent course exposure at similar going, but the fade-in-finish flag is a material concern in a race likely to collapse into a sprint; her true racing style is hold-up, shunted into midfield on the map by volume, and good-to-firm ground on a flat track amplifies that finishing problem.|
runners_data.comment: Questions remain over whether she truly stays this sort of trip, and a below-par effort in a handicap at Musselburgh last time, beaten 5 lengths, may have owed something to that. Best form has come around a mile on a sound surface, and she wears a hood for the first time today. Unreliable but clearly capable on her figures, and rates a leading contender.

runners_data.name: Dinah Myte
runners_data.note: Won over eight furlongs at Stamford on her penultimate start and steps up markedly to ten furlongs here, making the trip an unresolved question; she is a genuine backmarker placed into midfield by redistribution, and zero qualifying runs on similar good ground from her history (0W0P in sim-going) leaves her form profile the thinnest in the field on this surface.|
runners_data.comment: Won by a half-length off a 2lb lower mark at Newcastle two starts back, and clearly in good order round then, this filly ran into trouble at a vital stage when fourth last time, beaten 5 lengths off the same mark she carries today. She is effective around a mile and on softer ground, with the all-weather having proven tougher for her. Rated bottom of this field but not without recent claims.

races.paceDynamic: Saliko is the only confirmed pace-setter in this six-runner field, sliding forward from a natural hold-up role to set a lone, uncontested gallop over Nottingham's flat mile-and-two. With no genuine front-runner to push the tempo, the pace is likely to be measured and controlled, creating a falsely-run race that compresses the field and reduces the advantage of sitting off the pace. Good-to-firm ground rewards those with a sharp turn of foot rather than relentless galloping ability, meaning horses who can travel smoothly in the slipstream and quicken late are best positioned. This shape firmly favours prominent or mid-division horses who can quicken from a handy pitch — pure hold-up types relying on a strong pace to be set for them face a structural disadvantage here. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Huggable, Rosemary May, and Dinah Myte are all genuine backmarkers by inclination but are mapped to midfield, and in a steadily-run race they are unlikely to secure even that ground, making their finishing challenges harder to execute.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Saliko Leads, Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If Saliko sets a modest, uncontested gallop that keeps the field bunched and sets up a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Saliko bowls along comfortably in front on good-to-firm turf with no rival willing to pressurise, turning the race into a mile-and-two-furlong sprint from the home turn; horses who can travel close to the pace and pick up quickly hold a decisive edge over true hold-up types who need a genuine gallop to be set.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Movers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to string the field out but not so strong that closers can pounce, rewarding those who track Saliko within two lengths.
scenarios.body: Phaedra and any horse finding a handy pitch settle just behind Saliko and produce the most efficient trips, hitting the rising ground at the furlong pole with energy while the true backmarkers find themselves with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Saliko sets a stronger tempo than expected, perhaps hassled by a rival keen to get cover, genuinely stretching the field and creating a true test.
scenarios.body: A faster pace would suit the genuine hold-up horses if they can get within striking range turning in, with Phaedra's course-and-distance form and Celestias Comet's patient style theoretically benefiting — though the style-fit discounts on Huggable and Rosemary May mean their redistribution to midfield weakens this scenario's probability materially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Quickens Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Saliko, freed from any pressure, quickens decisively turning for home and steals a march on a field that has underestimated the gallop.
scenarios.body: Saliko's prominent tag and unchallenged lead could allow a front-running effort that the backmarkers simply cannot reel in on good-to-firm ground over this flat configuration; the style-fit discount applies as Saliko is a natural hold-up type pressed into leading, limiting confidence in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Saliko — watch her early, as any sign of reluctance or outright refusal to bowl along from the gate would leave this race with no genuine gallop and hand the race to whoever tracks from second.|

Huggable, Rosemary May, and Dinah Myte — all three true hold-up types will be hunting a position they may not naturally find in a slowly-run race; if the pace is modest, monitor whether they end up further back than their mapped positions suggest and effectively out of contention.|
Phaedra — recent runner eight days ago, which is a short turnaround; watch the paddock for any sign of residual flatness before assigning confidence to her course-and-distance profile.|

Rosemary May — the fade-in-finish flag combined with Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim and a compressed field means watch for her being produced wide into the straight, as lack of a pace target in front could expose the tendency to stop before the line.|

races.name: Last Orders Dash Handicap

runners_data.name: Regulus Black
runners_data.note: The race's dominant tactical asset — a confirmed prominent/front-runner who won over 10f on Good at Goodwood last time, fits both the trip and the ground ideally, and faces no pressure from any rival pacemaker; Hugo Palmer's 4/32 14-day strike rate is modest but the horse's own profile is exactly what this race shape rewards.
runners_data.comment: Won by two lengths at Chepstow two starts back and confirmed that promise when third, beaten just two lengths, up in trip last time on an unchanged mark. Now handicapping over middle distances with the yard in good form, he remains on a fair mark and rates the one to beat, even if he still needs to find that little extra to land this.

runners_data.name: Palace Artois
runners_data.note: William Haggas-trained hold-up type stepping up noticeably in trip from 8f, but its five-run form card shows a string of 5th-to-7th finishes on varying ground with zero wins or places, and the pace map offers nothing for it to track; the 12-day return is straightforward enough but the form says uplift is needed.
runners_data.comment: Undone for speed when beaten ten lengths in a Windsor handicap last time, but that run came at a shorter trip than ideal and today's step up should suit her finishing pace. First-time cheekpieces add further interest and she's proven on this going, though she needs to find plenty more than she's shown to be involved.

runners_data.name: Sound Gloria
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's runner has been beaten into 7th, 7th and 13th on its three career starts — all at 8f — and now faces both a trip extension and the challenge of closing down an uncontested front-runner; Harry Vigors' 5lb claim is a small offset, but the horse's natural hold-up style has been pushed into a midfield map slot and its finishing record offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Well held in a novice at Windsor latest under a stiffer test than she was ready for, but she's bred to appreciate more of a stamina test now handicapping. Form is sparse from just three starts, though improvement looks likely at this longer trip, and she remains of interest on a workable mark.

runners_data.name: Baldosa
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's runner does have a placed effort over 10f on Good going (2nd at Southwell) that is directly relevant to today's conditions; holds a natural hold-up profile that is squeezed into midfield in this race shape, and the 0/11 recent sim-going record illustrates consistent struggles to convert when the opportunity arises.
runners_data.comment: A maiden yet to get her head in front, but her form's plainly on the up, matching her true level when beaten just two lengths off an unchanged mark in a handicap at Wetherby last time. Proven over today's trip and going, she remains of interest for a leading threat, even with the yard currently out of winners.

runners_data.name: Alcanzor
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby runner with a "fades in finish" flag who has been 54 days off the track — the longest absence in the field — and whose three career runs all ended in double-digit or near-double-digit beaten positions; the 5lb claim from Rhys Elliott is a minor weight relief, but the hold-up profile displaced into midfield combined with the finishing tendency is a significant negative in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Down the field again without ever threatening in a novice at Catterick most recent, and with only three starts to his name the boost from stepping up in trip has yet to be tested. He's bred to be suited by today's longer distance, but on what he's shown he needs to progress plenty before he can be trusted.

runners_data.name: Enduring Story
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's 3yo has not finished better than 5th in six career starts, with all runs coming over 7f; today represents a clear trip extension for a horse whose hold-up style has been shuffled into a midfield slot by necessity, and William Pyle is a low-profile jockey whose book of rides rarely includes strong handicap form at this level.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten again in a handicap at Redcar latest, extending a run of poor form that's yet to show any encouragement, and the yard is similarly out of touch currently. Rock-bottom on our figures, she has plenty to prove before being taken seriously.

runners_data.name: Balmoral Boy
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 59 with JF Egan in the saddle — a clear upgrade in jockey quality — and this horse's best run of 3rd came over 8f on Soft; the step to 10f on fast ground is the key question mark, but as the highest-rated hold-up runner it profiles as the most credible chaser if Regulus Black falters, and Tinkler has the same 1/26 14-day record as with Baldosa, suggesting the yard is not in a purple patch.
runners_data.comment: Needs to bounce back after a below-par run at Wetherby latest, beaten six and a quarter lengths, with the yard also out of form currently. He does act on quick ground at today's trip, so he's not without claims, but the case for him goes only so far on these figures.

races.paceDynamic: Regulus Black is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 1m2f handicap and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to push it off its rhythm — it can stride to the front from stall one and control the tempo at a sensible, sustainable gallop on ground riding Good To Firm throughout the evening. The entire remainder of the field is composed of hold-up types, meaning Regulus Black will dictate every yard of the race, setting an honest but uncontested pace that is unlikely to be searingly fast over this trip. Five horses — Sound Gloria, Baldosa, Alcanzor, Enduring Story, and Palace Artois — are genuine hold-up types who will be chasing from off the pace, while Balmoral Boy brings the same profile with top weight; none of them can manufacture their ideal position because there is simply no pace battle to follow. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile: Regulus Black gets a soft lead, conserves energy and reaches the straight with a meaningful advantage over a field that will need to find competitive closing pace they have rarely demonstrated.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Regulus Black Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Regulus Black bowls to the front uncontested and is allowed to dictate a controlled, even tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Regulus Black, already proven at this trip over good ground (winning 10f at Goodwood), exploits the absence of any rival pacemaker, reaching the home straight with a clear lead and enough in reserve to hold on; its recent form of 1/10f/GOO is directly relevant and Palmer's runner fits the race shape perfectly. The hold-up horses face a stamina test closing down a horse that has not been softened up in any pace battle, and most of them have struggled to post top-speed finishes against run-of-the-mill opposition.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves faster than expected and causes Regulus Black to fade dramatically in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Balmoral Boy (OR 59, highest in the field) is the chief beneficiary if the front-runner ties up, given the extra distance (step to 10f) is an obvious progressive angle and Egan is a reliable big-race rider in these spots. Palace Artois or Baldosa could also arrive late, though both have largely posted mid-field finishes in shorter races and this trip on fast ground is an untested combination for them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If a second runner — most likely Balmoral Boy or Baldosa — pushes forward to challenge Regulus Black early, turning this into a two-horse pace duel.
scenarios.body: A contested front creates a stronger gallop, which could see a fresh closer benefit down the straight, but with so few natural hold-up horses having the engine to capitalise, the more likely outcome is that whoever travels prominently alongside Regulus Black sustains the effort better than those charging from deep. Balmoral Boy's step up in trip and Baldosa's handful of third-plus finishes at 10f suggest they are the two most capable of thriving if they commit to a prominent position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Overwhelm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the entire field settles off a strong gallop and multiple hold-up horses produce simultaneous late runs to overturn the front-runner.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Sound Gloria, Alcanzor or Enduring Story to produce form significantly better than their recent finishes suggest — Sound Gloria has been beaten 7th, 7th, 13th in three runs, Alcanzor carries a "fades in finish" flag, and Enduring Story has not finished better than 5th in six runs. The combination of out-of-role mapping, modest form figures and fast ground that rewards early-pace horses makes this the least credible shape.

watchPoints.text: Regulus Black's draw in stall 1 means it can immediately assert to the rail and lead with zero hassle — if it jumps cleanly, watch for it to establish a four-to-six length advantage before the first bend that may prove irreversible against this field.

Balmoral Boy is the one hold-up horse with genuine raw ratings headroom (OR 59) and Egan's presence is a significant tactical upgrade — watch whether Egan opts to push forward to track Regulus Black rather than settle deep, which would alter the entire complexion of the race.

Alcanzor's 54-day layoff combined with its flagged tendency to fade in finishes makes it a potential early withdrawal risk to monitor, and if it races prominently as a result of rustiness that could inject unexpected pace into the race.

Ground riding Good To Firm all evening at Nottingham — later races have consistently returned the same reading, confirming the surface is drying and quick; horses with good-ground form like Regulus Black (3W/P on similar) are better placed than those whose best form has come on Soft or Standard.

With five hold-up horses all needing to make ground from behind a sole front-runner, watch for crowding and traffic issues entering the home straight — Baldosa, Sound Gloria, Enduring Story and Palace Artois could all arrive at the same point simultaneously, meaning draw and early positioning within the chasing group will matter more than their raw finishing speed.

races.name: Construction Day 14th October Handicap

runners_data.name: Didaar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in a shape that offers limited opportunity for a late swooper; seven-pound claimer Jake Dickson takes the mount, trainer has a blank 14-day record (0/3), and the form string of 983-67 gives no reason to expect an improved showing at this trip.
runners_data.comment: A long-time maiden whose mark keeps easing, he wanted more pace to work with when beaten five lengths in a Newmarket handicap last time. The yard's in good form, he's drawn stall two, and first-time cheekpieces could be the change that finally gets him off the mark — he's a leading contender on our figures regardless.

runners_data.name: Holly Mist
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's filly is versatile in style and carries the headgear flag (b), which typically sharpens early focus; her four-placing consistency at 8-12f and a recent top-three on similar ground makes her a genuine player for a race in which a steady pace suits a genuine stayer, though similar-going figures (1/8) are modest.
runners_data.comment: Consistency has been the hallmark of her recent starts, and she matched her true form when beaten just three and a quarter lengths off a 1lb higher mark at Doncaster last time. The trainer's in excellent touch, the mark continues to ease, and first-time blinkers could sharpen her up further at a trip she handles well.

runners_data.name: Time Turner
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old won over 12f on Standard and placed at 10f in similar ground conditions; Paul Mulrennan provides a significant booking upgrade and the hood (v) suggests a settled, economical traveller — his profile as a hold-up horse with proven stamina fits a measured-pace scenario better than most.
runners_data.comment: A slow-away sort who had too much lost ground to make up when beaten a length and a quarter off a 1lb higher mark at Musselburgh last time, a fair effort back from a break. Generally holds his form and is proven at today's trip and going, but the first-time visor points to early speed as his main issue.

runners_data.name: Stipulation
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's confirmed pace-setter will have the race run to suit early but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a quiet caution — this horse is most effective making the running, and if anything disturbs that role its chance deflates sharply; one win from fifteen on similar going is worth noting.
runners_data.comment: A picture of consistency with three thirds on the spin, his latest Windsor defeat coming only after trouble in running for a rise of just 2lb since. Suited by today's trip and ground, with cheekpieces added for the first time, he rates the one to beat on our figures, even though he had nothing extra to offer once the trouble cleared last time.

runners_data.name: Into Combat
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's runner is a true hold-up horse mapped forward here only because of overcrowding at the rear; a fading pattern at the finish (⚠) and an 0/6 record on similar ground make this difficult to recommend, and the STYLE_FIT flag confirms it is not racing in its optimal position.
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths in a Newmarket handicap last time when outpowered for speed, though that effort may have owed something to needing the run. Solid enough at today's trip and going, but with no big placing efforts in his last five and form that's genuinely hard to assess, he's tough to trust with confidence.

runners_data.name: Danehill Star
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old has five places from fifteen on similar going and is the most active runner in this field (13 days since last run); a natural closer repositioned to midfield on the map, it is the best-credentialled of the redistributed hold-up horses and may actually claim a forward position given its recent form figures of 221433.
runners_data.comment: A model of consistency with a win and four places from his last six starts, only nudged out late when beaten a length and a half off an unchanged mark at Brighton last time. Effective at today's trip on quick ground, with first-time cheekpieces added, he takes plenty of catching but still needs more to reverse placings with the principals.

runners_data.name: Pride Eye
runners_data.note: A 124-day break is a significant concern for Mark Rimell's four-year-old, and the horse has a well-documented tendency to fade in the closing stages (⚠); its entire recent history comes on Standard ground, so this Good to Firm surface is genuinely untested, and its natural hold-up style is doubly compromised by redistribution.
runners_data.comment: Yet to find genuine consistency in a short career, and turf today is new ground after all her starts on the all-weather. Beaten seven and a half lengths at Kempton last time with nothing to blame, and having been off the track for four months, she's hard to fancy despite the first-time tongue-tie offering some change of tactics.

runners_data.name: Quirke On Parole
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's four-year-old carries the lowest OR in the race (50) and its best recent finishes have come over shorter distances on Good or Standard; placed in similar-going races (3P from 12) but the step into this shape — as a natural closer forced into midfield — reduces its chance of being in the right place at the right time.
runners_data.comment: Forced the pace more than ideal when beaten seven lengths in a Beverley handicap last time, and she's now below the mark that last yielded a win, needing to rediscover that form. Proven at today's trip, but with little consistency across her last five starts, she's hard to trust without more signs of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Stipulation is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press from the front, should be allowed to dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 1m2f Nottingham flat on Good to Firm ground. The tempo will be honest but controlled, and with Stipulation able to roll along at its own pace, the race is likely to develop into a test of which runners can sustain their effort through the final two furlongs rather than one that is truly end-to-end. The absence of early pressure means that midfield and hold-up horses will need either a well-timed move from Paul Mulrennan or Harry Vigors's camp, or a genuine stamina edge, to haul in a front-runner that never gets into trouble. This shape strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield progressive stayer who can travel smoothly behind a measured pace and produce a sustained, rather than a sudden, finishing effort — Time Turner and Holly Mist fit that profile most cleanly. Note that Into Combat, Danehill Star, Pride Eye, and Quirke On Parole are all genuine hold-up types who have been mapped forward on the visual because more true closers exist than the map can accommodate at the rear — Stipulation is most likely to secure the front, and Danehill Star is the only redistributed runner with the early-race positioning to realistically challenge for a prominent berth.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stipulation Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Stipulation takes up the lead unchallenged and sets a true but measured gallop that suits a well-organised race on fast ground.
scenarios.body: Stipulation rolls along in front, the field settles into a processional shape, and the horse with the best cruising speed and stamina combination picks it off only in the closing stages — or Stipulation itself holds on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Stayer Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady early and a well-positioned midfield horse produces a sustained run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A controlled early gallop compresses the field and the runner who travels best through the race without burning energy sweeps past a tiring front-runner; the 1m2f trip and Good to Firm surface reward clean, economical racing.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stipulation Outstays All Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Stipulation's hold on the pace proves so comfortable that no rival can mount a meaningful challenge in the straight.
scenarios.body: Having never been headed or pressured, Stipulation simply extends its lead into the final furlong and the field, packed with natural hold-up types asked to race prominently, cannot produce the necessary turn of foot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Late Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and creates enough of a gap for a genuine closer to thread through late.
scenarios.body: A horse forced to settle further back than ideal — Danehill Star or Quirke On Parole — finds a clear run at the furlong pole and finishes fastest of all on this sound surface, though the compressed field and single pace-setter make this the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether any runner challenges Stipulation for the lead in the first two furlongs — if Into Combat or Danehill Star push forward unexpectedly, the pace dynamic changes entirely and hold-up horses gain a more realistic winning chance.

Time Turner's headgear (visor) and Paul Mulrennan booking is the standout jockey-trainer combination in the race — if he travels smoothly in the first half mile, he warrants close attention rounding the home turn.

Pride Eye's 124-day absence and unproven form on Good to Firm ground make it a risk to follow; if it shows signs of rustiness or fails to stride out freely early, it is likely out of contention before the straight.

Danehill Star is the most active and consistent of the hold-up horses — if Tony Carroll has freshened it for this 13-day turnaround and it secures a forward berth rather than its natural rear position, it becomes more dangerous than its OR of 59 suggests.

The going report consistently reads Good to Firm for this 1m2f slot — conditions are faster than the declared Good, which will suit those who can quicken and may expose any runners that struggle to handle the quicker surface, particularly Holly Mist whose recent outings have come on Soft or Standard.
